This is a place beyond compare.
This is King’s
The King’s School is actually three schools – The Senior School, Junior King’s and The King’s School International College. All three are located in, or near, the historic City of Canterbury and just an hour from London. We’re co-educational, offer boarding or day schooling and welcome pupils from the ages of 3 through to 18. Whichever school you choose, they are all The King’s School; united by a remarkable legacy, situated in a beautiful part of England and sharing an open and inclusive culture.

Partnerships & Outreach
We have two overall objectives when it comes to partnerships: raising aspirations and widening horizons.
Pupils’ prospects are improved when schools collaborate to enrich teaching and learning. They also gain greater understanding by interacting with children from different backgrounds and learning beyond the curriculum.
This is why we are a member of EKST (East Kent Schools Together), an innovative independent and state school partnership in which each school contributes to and draws from the process equally. For pupils, it’s about meeting new people and learning new skills – with the ultimate aim of improving confidence, resilience, well-being and a sense of community.
Saturday Smarties. A fun Science programme with more than twenty local state primary schools. Its main aim is to broaden pupils’ experiences of science in a lab setting.
Sounding Out. A classical music programme involving pupils from five partner primary schools. They have access to fully funded one-to-one lessons in the violin or trumpet each week, as well as masterclasses and concerts.
Masterclasses at our Malthouse Theatre. A series of performing arts workshops, activities and masterclasses.
Volunteering. Older King’s pupils volunteer at local primary schools to assist with language classes and reading. They also volunteer locally working with charities, supporting events, and generally being a positive presence in the wider community.
Saturday Smarties
King’s offers science masterclasses for Year 5 and 6 pupils from primary schools in and around Canterbury as part of its Canterbury Primary Science Partnership.
Sounding Out
In September 2019, we launched Sounding Out, a revolutionary programme to provide lessons in orchestral instruments, without the barrier of cost, to children at all the city primary schools in Canterbury.

pageCache.text:

Other Projects
Partnership projects offer many mutual benefits, enabling our pupils to develop valuable leadership and organisational skills as they contribute to the smooth running of events and enabling them to broaden their own experience and the experiences of other young people.
King’s hosts an annual event called Minilympics, a day of exciting sporting activities for local primary schools.
180 Year 4 pupils come to Birley’s playing fields and, in teams of mixed schools, are given sessions on cricket (in association with Kent cricket), field testing and team athletics, as well as a talk on healthy eating and an opportunity to meet Olympic sports stars.
Each child attending receives a medal and T shirt and trophies are awarded for team spirit. A delicious barbecue lunch is provided and the day is kindly sponsored by local businesses. One parent who attended with his son’s school said “an exciting and engaging day was had by every child. The commitment and organisation were second to none”.
Drama teachers and pupils from local schools join us in our state-of-the-art Malthouse Theatre for a series of masterclasses, engaging in acting activities as well as workshops focusing on artistic performance.
Feedback from a local teacher: Thank you so much for today. The students loved it and got a lot from the workshops. I genuinely think this was the best workshop I have taken students to. Both practitioners were engaging and had great activities for the students. Both gave practical [takeaways] that the students could use and helped the students build confidence. The theatre is stunning, and a fantastic space and the lunch provided was delicious. Great day! Thank you again for the opportunity.
Pupil volunteers from King’s assist with language classes and reading lessons at local primary schools each week.
Our volunteering contingent continues to grow with pupils assisting not only in local schools but also in the wider community: working with charities, taking part in local events, and being a positive presence in the local community.

Nursery & Pre-Prep – Friday 9 October 2026

Saturday Smarties
King’s offers science masterclasses for Year 5 and 6 pupils from primary schools in and around Canterbury as part of its Canterbury Primary Science Partnership.
The aim is to broaden experiences of science in lab settings and give the pupils an immersive feel for the various science subjects. These “Saturday Smarties” pupils, selected by their schools on the basis of interest and ability, attend sessions across the year, each of which focuses on a different scientific theme. Recent sessions have looked at forensic investigation with pupils learning how to lift fingerprints, analyse blood and soil samples and look at dental imprints to discover the many ways that science can help solve crimes.
Running for over ten years, over 500 pupils have been part of the Saturday Smarties programme and our feedback has shown that many have been inspired to consider studying science later on at university. As a Year 5 boy from one local school said after one session: “This is the day I became a scientist.”
Sounding Out
In September 2019, we launched Sounding Out, a revolutionary programme to provide lessons in orchestral instruments, without the barrier of cost, to children at all the city primary schools in Canterbury.

pageCache.text:
Nursery & Pre-Prep – Friday 9 October 2026
Junior School – Saturday 10 October 2026
Sounding Out
We believe that instrumental lessons should be available to all children so, in September 2019, we launched Sounding Out, a revolutionary programme to provide lessons in orchestral instruments, without the barrier of cost, to children at all the city primary schools in Canterbury.
Supported by King’s and a wide network of benefactors, our goal is simple: to break down the barriers and open up the opportunity of music to the widest catchment possible. Our ambition is to develop a community music base at King’s that will thrive in years to come and bring participants together with King’s pupils.
While many schools offer excellent schemes for ensemble participation, Sounding Out puts instruments in children’s hands for the first time, seeking to reverse the decline in classical tuition amongst young people in the UK. A typical morning will include an instrumental lesson on either the violin or trumpet (with expansion to other instruments in our development plan) and a group musicianship session. Pupils are loaned their own instrument to take home, and given all resources, including sheet music and a music bag.
Support Us
Generous donations have helped support King’s for many years, providing pupils with fee assistance and contributing to the development of state-of-the-art facilities, including the Malthouse Theatre and Rausing Science Centre.
Partnership Projects
Partnership projects offer many mutual benefits, enabling all pupils to develop valuable leadership and organisational skills.

pageCache.text:
Nursery & Pre-Prep – Friday 9 October 2026
Junior School – Saturday 10 October 2026
Pastoral Care
We take pride in our outstanding pastoral care – the safeguarding and wellbeing of our pupils has always been paramount, and the Senior School is structured to support this.
Each pupil, Boarding or Day, is a member of a House; the centre of their school life, and in many cases a home from home. Each House is under the supportive care of a Housemaster or Housemistress and includes a Matron or Pastoral Care Assistant and a dedicated Tutor Team. All academic staff are attached to a certain House as tutors, and each tutor group consists of approximately 10 pupils. This system has been in place since 1886 and it creates very strong bonds between tutors and pupils.
We also have a well-equipped health centre, staffed by fully qualified nurses providing 24-hour care during term, as well as a team of qualified counsellors and a Life Coach. Our Chaplaincy team – responsible for worship, assemblies and Cathedral services – are also available to both staff and pupils as advisors and counsellors.
In general, pupils feel nourished and supported by a school culture that is open, warm and inclusive, and all are encouraged to support each other; to celebrate the success of everyone, as well as their own.
Co-curricular
King’s excels not only academically, but also in developing skills and achievements beyond the curriculum.

Careers at King’s
The King’s School is a supportive and welcoming community working across five sites in and around the historic city of Canterbury. From senior academic leaders to members of the extensive support services, all of our colleagues play a key role in supporting our pupils, both local and international, to experience an exceptional King’s education.
The School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of its young people and expects all employees and volunteers to share this commitment. Any offer of employment will be subject to an enhanced DBS disclosure.
We are an inclusive employer and recognise the benefits that diversity brings to the work environment. We welcome applications from a wide range of candidates. Selection for positions at King’s will be based on individual merit.
Pension The school offers a generous defined contribution salary sacrifice pension scheme with the option of enhanced contributions.
Life Assurance All employees are automatically enrolled into a life assurance scheme that pays benefits to dependents.
Enhanced family leave entitlements The school support colleagues to balance work and life and offer enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption benefits.
Medical Insurance Full comprehensive medical insurance is available to eligible employees.
Employee Assistance Programme A free confidential helpline available 7 days a week, 365 days a year and the option of accessing face to face counselling.
Sports Centre All employees have gold membership with access to the pool, gym and other facilities.
Cycle to Work Scheme The school operate a salary sacrifice cycle scheme which could provide savings of up to 40%, dependent on salary and cycle cost.
Eye Care Regular VDU users can receive a financial contribution to the cost of both eye tests and glasses.
Financial Advice King’s facilitates regular free impartial financial advice to all employees.
Free Lunch (if eligible) The catering department provides varied and high-quality meals at no cost during term time.
Teaching staff receive all the benefits listed above, as well as –
Subsidised accommodation Eligible Teachers will qualify for subsidised accommodation for the first two years of employment at below market rates.
Fee Remission Access to generous fee remission for children of teachers to attend at King’s and Junior King’s.
Pension Option to join either the Teacher’s Pension Scheme or the Defined Contribution Scheme (with 23.6% employer contribution to either).

Staff & Governors
Senior Leadership

The International College
Anne Pujadas-Telmon
Co-Head
Anne Pujadas-Telmon joined The King’s School International College in January 2025 as Assistant Principal then Acting Joint Principal before becoming Co-Head.
Born in France, Anne first came to England at the age of 16, before returning to complete a degree and later undertaking a PGCE in Canterbury. She began her teaching career at Sir Roger Manwood’s Grammar School in Sandwich, where she remained for 25 years and progressed to Senior Assistant Headteacher. During this time, she held a wide range of roles, including Boarding Tutor, Head of Department and Head of Year, gaining extensive experience across both academic, boarding and pastoral areas of school life.
As a native French speaker who has experienced studying abroad herself, Anne has a strong understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing international students, particularly in developing confidence in English and adapting to life in a UK school. She brings a clear commitment and excellence to high-quality teaching and student development.
In her spare time, she enjoys sport, particularly golf and tennis, as well as exploring the world.
The International College
Carl Lyon
Co-Head
Carl Lyon joined the International College in 2020, with responsibility for pastoral development, student wellbeing, extra-curricular opportunities, and enhancing the overall student experience.
With almost 30 years of experience in education, Carl has taught in several prestigious schools across the UK and internationally. In 2008, he became a founding Housemaster at Repton Dubai, helping to establish the school’s pastoral culture and community ethos. Beyond the classroom, he has led numerous initiatives designed to enrich school life, including developing overseas partnerships between schools, organising large-scale open days, and creating memorable events such as the Sixth Form Leavers’ Ball.
A passionate advocate for educational research and innovation, Carl completed a Doctorate in Education in 2025. His research focused on improving outcomes for learners and strengthening student engagement, interests that continue to shape his professional practice. He is also an established educational author. Having co-authored several educational textbooks, he celebrated the publication of his first solo book in 2026, published by Routledge, focusing on more able learners and the importance of elevating the student voice within education.
His commitment to providing exceptional opportunities for young people is reflected in the breadth of his work. He has organised charity fundraising events involving running, rowing, and parachute jumping; sourced England badminton players to coach school teams; arranged specialist martial arts training for younger students; attended adventure training programmes; and trekked across the Indian Himalayas.

Pupils at The King’s School Canterbury are celebrating success following the publication of this year’s A level examination results.
Across the cohort, and before reviews of marking, more than 80% of all grades were awarded at A*-B, while 63% of pupils achieved the “gold standard” of AAB or better, providing a strong foundation for progression to competitive university courses and other ambitious next steps. Almost a quarter of all grades awarded were at the coveted A* grade and over half achieved A* or A, reflecting the excellent achievements of pupils across a wide range of subjects.
This year’s results continue King’s longstanding tradition of academic excellence while highlighting the breadth of achievement across the cohort. Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions your family will make, and our role is to make that process as smooth as possible.
Year 9 is the largest point of entry into King’s, with approximately 150 pupils joining each year at this stage. We also have a healthy intake of 50-60 pupils coming to the school at Year 12.
King’s is a fast-paced school, both academically and in terms of the co-curricular offering. It is important that children are able to cope with that fast pace, but individual character and circumstance, together with ability to contribute widely to the extensive range of co-curricular activities are also taken into consideration.
Many pupils come to us from UK prep schools, including Junior King’s, but a good number also join from other UK schools and from schools around the globe. The school prides itself on its diversity and on its focus on the individual.
Our Admissions team are very much here to help you with any questions as regards the whole process of entry to King’s for your son or daughter. Please contact us by phone or by email to discuss further.

Pupils enter King’s at Year 9 from a large number of prep schools. The majority of these prep schools are in the UK, though some are overseas.

For any admissions queries, please contact the Admissions Team – admissions@kings-school.co.uk
Individual visits include a tour of the school with a current pupil and a meeting with the Director of Admissions or another senior member of staff at King’s. Open Days are also held on a Saturday morning in September & May. Dates and other details are published on the website in advance.
It is necessary to register a prospective pupil for entry at an early stage in the admissions process in order to confirm your interest in a place. This can be done at any age and once a pupil is registered, parents will receive regular updates keeping them informed about the school. The registration fee is currently £200+VAT.
Pupils sit the ISEB Pre-Test at their current school in the Autumn Term of Year 6 and then, on the strength of those results, will be invited to King’s for an Experience Day in the February of Year 6. Offers are made in March of Year 6 on the basis of performance at the ISEB Pre-Test, formal reference from the pupil’s current school and their time at the Experience Day.
A place is confirmed through the payment of a deposit following the offer of a place.
Following your confirmation of acceptance, we will invite your child to a Taster Day in the Spring of Year 8, allowing them to get to know some of their fellow pupils, King’s teachers and the Housemaster or Housemistress.

Nursery & Pre-Prep – Friday 9 October 2026
Junior School – Saturday 10 October 2026
Begin Your Year 7 Adventure
Year 7 is an exciting time full of new opportunities, new friendships and new challenges. At Junior King’s, pupils join a nurturing top of school environment where they can lead, explore and grow before moving on to The King’s School Canterbury in Year 9.
Learning That Goes Beyond the Classroom – Our beautiful riverside site inspires hands on learning, adventure and discovery. Pupils enjoy a rich mix of academics, outdoor learning, sport, music, drama and inter house activities which give every child the chance to find their place and flourish.
A Broad, Dynamic Curriculum – Our Year 7 curriculum is designed to stretch, support and spark curiosity. From creative subjects to critical thinking, pupils build strong foundations and grow in confidence during these key transition years. Read our Curriculum Books below:
Year 7 Curriculum Year 8 Curriculum
Pastoral Care That Truly Knows Your Child – Year 7 pupils are supported by staff who understand them deeply. Our dedicated pastoral team ensures each child feels safe, valued and encouraged, helping them navigate the early teen years with confidence.
A Seamless Journey to The King’s School Canterbury – Junior King’s is the beginning of a remarkable educational pathway. Many pupils benefit from a through offer to King’s, giving families confidence and clarity from the moment they join us. Our close partnership with King’s ensures a smooth and seamless transition for every child.
The Advantage of Being at the Top of a Prep School – In Years 7 and 8, pupils become leaders, not new starters. With greater responsibility and visibility, they develop independence, resilience and character at a vital stage of growth.
A Co-Curricular Life Full of Opportunity – From orchestras, choirs and drama to sport, outdoor pursuits and clubs, our vibrant co-curricular programme helps pupils discover passions, develop teamwork and build lifelong interests.
Junior King’s offers several entry points for pupils. For those leaving their schools at the end of Year 6, we can provide a through place to The King’s School Canterbury, subject to a strong performance in the assessment process and a positive reference from their current school. This pathway includes Years 7 and 8 at Junior King’s, followed by a seamless transition to the Senior School in Year 9.
For Year 7 entry, Junior King’s offers two Academic Scholarships and two Academic Exhibitions to outstanding internal and external candidates who demonstrate academic excellence and significant future potential. For further information, please visit our Scholarships page to explore the opportunities available.
Our Admissions team is very much here to help you with any questions you may have.
We offer day, occasional, flexi and full boarding, giving families genuine choice and flexibility. Pupils can board regularly, stay just on the days that help busiest family schedules, or attend as day pupils. Whatever option they choose, every child becomes part of our warm and supportive community, enjoying a reassuring home from home where they feel settled, known and cared for.
A parent whose daughter joined Junior King’s in Year 7 reflects on their first year, sharing early impressions, key highlights, and how the school supported her transition and growth, offering a fresh perspective on joining our community from Year 7.
Getting to and from school is simple and secure thanks to the dedicated transport options available to our pupils. We offer an accompanied train service between Wye and Sturry, led by our Assistant Tutors who ensure pupils travel safely each day. This service operates Monday to Friday with stops at Wye, Chilham, Chartham and Canterbury West, and includes a return journey at the end of the school day.
In addition, King’s runs a fleet of branded minibuses serving local areas across Kent, including Faversham, Whitstable, Herne Bay, Ramsgate, Broadstairs, Margate, Whitfield, Bridge, Deal, Ash and Wingham. All minibus drivers are King’s employees with advanced DBS checks, giving families peace of mind that pupils are in safe and reliable hands throughout their journey.

“They’ve got it all here, and we can’t think of many more inspiring places to learn.”
While the majority of our Year 8 pupils move on to the Senior School, some do move on to local grammar schools and other independent schools around the country.
We work closely with parents, giving personal and professional advice, and, by understanding each pupil’s needs, we ensure that the chosen secondary school is the most appropriate setting for their future success.

To ease congestion, support the environment, and assist parents, Junior King’s offers a range of transport services.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome • The King's School Canterbury
pageCache.text:
Nursery & Pre-Prep – Friday 9 October 2026
Junior School – Saturday 10 October 2026
Head’s Welcome
It is an enormous privilege and pleasure to lead this remarkable school.
Set in a breathtaking location amongst the precincts of Canterbury Cathedral, our school offers an environment and experience like no other. Believed to be the first school in England and located in a bustling, historic city and world heritage site, our school has a unique history and our community a special character: spiritually aware, connected, warm-hearted and open-minded.
Ms Jude Lowson, Head of The King’s School Canterbury
We are inspired not constrained by tradition, and this is a school which has always looked to the future. Today, pupils benefit from fantastic facilities, a wide-ranging, enlightening and stimulating curriculum, a phenomenal breadth of co-curricular activities and outstanding pastoral care. This is a place which ignites passions and nurtures individual interests, no matter what they are, allowing pupils to forge their own unique path whilst with us, and preparing them for fulfilling futures, regardless of the course that they follow beyond school.
Ms Lowson joined the school in Autumn 2023 and brings with her a wide range of experience from both co-educational and single-sex day and boarding schools, most recently as the Senior Deputy Head of King’s College School, Wimbledon.
Growing up in Belgium, she was educated at Sevenoaks School and the University of Cambridge, where she gained a Masters in History and a Diploma in Management Studies. She worked as a strategist in one of the UK’s leading advertising agencies before beginning her teaching career at Whitgift School in Croydon.
Ms Lowson is married and her daughter attends Junior King’s. In her spare time, she is a novice saxophonist, and enjoys cycling and running on the many beautiful routes in the Kent countryside surrounding Canterbury.
“The cathedral, visible from every point of the campus, has a profound impact on the school and provides one of the most inspiring settings for a school.”
Academic
The King’s education is designed to encompass both depth and breadth.

pageCache.text:
Nursery & Pre-Prep – Friday 9 October 2026
Junior School – Saturday 10 October 2026
School Transport Service
The King’s School operates a fleet of branded minibuses, enabling local pupils to travel safely to and from our Schools.
All our minibus drivers are King’s School employees with advanced DBS checks, offering parents peace of mind knowing that their children will arrive at school safely and on time.
Pick-up/drop-off points include:
Ash Broadstairs Canterbury West Train Station Deal Faversham Margate Minster Preston Ramsgate Teynham Westbrook Whitstable Wingham
To support families with pupils returning to the School after a weekend or exeat at home, King’s have partnered with Vectare to offer a weekly bus service from locations in Kent and London.
Initially, we are running two services every Sunday evening. One from Clapham Common and one from Tunbridge Wells. Vectare manage all aspects of the school’s service and bookings can made via their website, accessible via the link below.
At the end of each term and half term, the School operates a minibus service to London Heathrow Airport. The cost of the service is £30 per passenger which will be recharged on their school account after the service has taken place. Each pupil is allowed two medium sized suitcases and a carry on only.
Parents can enquire about the service and book a seat by contacting: c.watson@kings-school.co.uk | 01227 595739 / 07483979212, or they can contact their respective House Matron or Pastoral Care Assistant to book a seat.
There is the possibility of running return services, although is dependent on arrival times and demand. Please contact: c.watson@kings-school.co.uk if you would like to inquire about this, along with information about flight timing and arrival terminals.

From Nursery through to Sixth Form. We have multiple entry points for pupils aged 3-18 across our three schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History • The King's School Canterbury
pageCache.text:
Nursery & Pre-Prep – Friday 9 October 2026
Junior School – Saturday 10 October 2026
History
The King’s School, our Senior School, is widely regarded as the oldest school in England.
Its story is intertwined with that of the United Kingdom’s first cathedral, Canterbury Cathedral, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
St Augustine arrived in 597 on a mission from Rome to convert the Anglo-Saxons. Canterbury Cathedral and St Augustine’s Abbey were then founded and education emerged as one role of these monastic establishments. Schools existed for many centuries until the Dissolution of the Monasteries. In 1541 a Royal Charter from Henry VIII reorganised the Cathedral and provided for a School with fifty scholars. Since then, the King’s School, as it became known, has survived the upheaval of the English Civil War and the Second World War, when it was evacuated to Cornwall. Throughout all this time it has continued to grow and evolve to become the globally respected seat of learning it is today.
“I think it’s wonderful that pupils here are connected to the history and the heritage of this place.”
Junior King’s was founded in 1879 and spent its first 50 years within the Canterbury Cathedral Precincts before moving to the idyllic village of Sturry, just two miles from Canterbury. It was opened there in 1929 by the famed Nobel Prize winning author, Rudyard Kipling.
The King’s School International College is our most recent arrival, opening its doors in 2018. Housed in an award-winning building, it welcomes international pupils with truly state-of-the facilities and, of course, world class teaching.
“The school and surroundings are steeped in history.”
Canterbury
Canterbury is a fantastic place to live and learn. It’s a city with a fascinating history and a vibrant atmosphere.
